Ostia Antica — Rome, Italy

🟡 Local press research

Average day Average night

In detail

Ostia Antica is Rome's ancient Roman port city, one of Italy's best-preserved archaeological parks, alongside a small modern borgo across the road with a medieval castle, cafés and shops. The fenced, ticketed archaeological site itself is well supervised and safe to visit; no incidents involving tourists inside the ruins were found. However, local outlets reported repeated 2026 coverage of an escalation of car break-ins, attempted burglaries of homes and shops, and muggings in the surrounding residential streets, with shopkeepers describing opening at dawn without any police patrol passing and residents describing themselves as terrorized. This is a real, recurring, multi-outlet documented problem in the modern town rather than the archaeological park.
